topic: Tantraloka ahnika 09: Tattvādhvā — the 36 categories, cause/effect, succession
moves: Presents the tattvādhvā (path of categories) within the sixfold adhvā scheme, enumerating the 36 tattvas from Śiva down to pṛthivī
Analyzes cause/effect (kāraṇa/kārya) relations among the tattvas, distinguishing levels of manifestation
Treats succession (krama) in the emanation/involution of categories, not as mere temporal sequence
Situates the 36-tattva scheme against Sāṃkhya's 25 and other Śaiva enumerations
Operates within the worldview block (ch.1–13), before the ritual/initiation block (ch.14–37)
traps: Tattvādhvā vs. the other five adhvans (mantrādhvā, kalādhvā, padādhvā, varṇādhvā, bhuvanādhvā) — do not conflate paths
36 tattvas vs. 25 Sāṃkhya tattvas — different enumerations, different ontological commitments
Cause/effect (kāraṇa/kārya) vs. mere temporal succession (krama) — krama here is ontological ordering
Śiva-tattva vs. Sadāśiva/Īśvara/Sadvidyā — adjacent high tattvas easily blurred
Print/edition variants between Dyczkowski (with Jayaratha's Viveka), Gnoli, and older editions; verse numbering may shift
Lakshmanjoo's oral teaching is a horizon, not a citable source for the text's claims
approach: Scope to ahnika 09 only; do not import ritual material from ch.14–37
Cite via Dyczkowski's edition with Jayaratha's Viveka; note Gnoli for Italian tradition
Mark gaps where excerpts are thin rather than reconstructing from memory
Distinguish Abhinavagupta's voice from Jayaratha's commentary
Flag any verse-number or reading uncertainty explicitly
